title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 61 (Power of Limited Company to Alter Its Share Capital)

content.overview: Section 61 permits a limited company having a share capital, if so authorised by its articles, to alter its memorandum in general meeting to: (a) increase authorised share capital; (b) consolidate and divide share capital into shares of a larger amount (Tribunal approval required where the consolidation or division changes the voting percentage of shareholders); (c) convert fully paid-up shares into stock and reconvert that stock into fully paid-up shares of any denomination; (d) sub-divide shares into shares of a smaller amount while keeping the proportion between the amount paid and the amount unpaid on each reduced share the same as in the share from which it is derived; or (e) cancel shares that have not been taken or agreed to be taken and diminish the amount of share capital by the amount of the shares so cancelled. Cancellation under sub-section (1) is not deemed a reduction of share capital.
content.glance: Articles-authorised alteration of capital in general meeting: increase authorised; consolidate/divide (Tribunal if voting % changes); convert to/from stock; sub-divide preserving paid/unpaid proportion; cancel unissued. Cancel ≠ reduction.
content.study: A limited company having a share capital may, if so authorised by its articles, alter its memorandum in its general meeting under section 61(1) to—(a) increase its authorised share capital by such amount as it thinks expedient; (b) consolidate and divide all or any of its share capital into shares of a larger amount than its existing shares, provided that no consolidation and division which results in changes in the voting percentage of shareholders shall take effect unless approved by the Tribunal on an application made in the prescribed manner; (c) convert all or any of its fully paid-up shares into stock, and reconvert that stock into fully paid-up shares of any denomination; (d) sub-divide its shares, or any of them, into shares of smaller amount than is fixed by the memorandum, so that in the sub-division the proportion between the amount paid and the amount, if any, unpaid on each reduced share shall be the same as it was in the case of the share from which the reduced share is derived; or (e) cancel shares which, at the date of the passing of the resolution in that behalf, have not been taken or agreed to be taken by any person, and diminish the amount of its share capital by the amount of the shares so cancelled. Section 61(2) provides that the cancellation of shares under sub-section (1) shall not be deemed to be a reduction of share capital. Current-law framing: confirm articles authority; identify the exact clause (a)–(e); apply the Tribunal proviso only where consolidation or division changes voting percentage; preserve the paid/unpaid proportion on sub-division; treat cancel of unissued shares as outside the reduction procedure; file the notice required by section 64 where applicable.

sections.heading: Authorised alterations (s. 61(1)(a)–(e))
sections.body: Increase authorised capital; consolidate and divide (with Tribunal proviso); convert fully paid shares into stock and reconvert; sub-divide preserving paid/unpaid proportion; cancel unissued shares — if the articles authorise and the company acts in general meeting.

sections.heading: Tribunal approval (proviso to s. 61(1)(b))
sections.body: No consolidation and division that results in changes in the voting percentage of shareholders shall take effect unless approved by the Tribunal on an application made in the prescribed manner.

sections.heading: Sub-division proportion rule (s. 61(1)(d))
sections.body: On sub-division the proportion between the amount paid and the amount, if any, unpaid on each reduced share must remain the same as in the share from which the reduced share is derived.

sections.heading: Cancel not reduction (s. 61(2))
sections.body: Cancellation of shares under sub-section (1) shall not be deemed to be a reduction of share capital.

provisions.title: Power of limited company to alter its share capital

examples.title: Increase of authorised capital
examples.body: Articles authorise. The company in general meeting increases authorised capital under s. 61(1)(a). No Tribunal approval is required for a pure increase.

examples.title: Consolidation affecting voting percentage
examples.body: Consolidation of shares would change the voting percentages of shareholders. Under the proviso to s. 61(1)(b) the alteration does not take effect unless approved by the Tribunal.

examples.title: Sub-division preserving proportion
examples.body: A Rs 100 share on which Rs 60 is paid is sub-divided into two Rs 50 shares. Each reduced share must carry Rs 30 paid and Rs 20 unpaid so that the paid/unpaid proportion remains the same (s. 61(1)(d)).

hypotheticals.question: Does cancelling unissued shares under s. 61 require the reduction procedure under s. 66?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 61(2) expressly provides that cancellation of shares under sub-section (1) shall not be deemed to be a reduction of share capital.

hypotheticals.question: When is Tribunal approval required for a consolidation under s. 61?
hypotheticals.analysis: Only where the consolidation or division results in changes in the voting percentage of shareholders (proviso to s. 61(1)(b)). A consolidation that does not alter voting percentages does not engage the proviso.

distinctions.title: Alteration of capital (s. 61) vs reduction of capital (s. 66)
distinctions.left: Articles-based structural changes including cancel of unissued shares; general-meeting power; Tribunal only for voting-percentage change on consolidate/divide
distinctions.right: Tribunal-supervised reduction of issued capital with creditor safeguards and confirmation procedure

rows.left: Permitted under s. 61(1)(e); not deemed reduction (s. 61(2))
rows.right: Reduction procedure not applicable to pure cancel of unissued under s. 61

misconceptions.trap: Any capital change under s. 61 needs Tribunal approval.
misconceptions.correction: Tribunal approval is required only where consolidation or division under s. 61(1)(b) results in a change in the voting percentage of shareholders.

misconceptions.trap: Sub-division can freely alter the paid/unpaid ratio on the reduced shares.
misconceptions.correction: Section 61(1)(d) requires that the proportion between the amount paid and the amount unpaid on each reduced share remain the same as in the original share.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 61 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Confirm the company is a limited company with share capital and that the articles authorise the alteration. II. Identify the exact clause of s. 61(1)(a)–(e) relied on. III. If consolidation or division is proposed, test whether voting percentage of shareholders changes; if yes, Tribunal approval under the proviso is required. IV. If sub-division is proposed, apply the paid/unpaid proportion rule in s. 61(1)(d). V. Note that cancel of unissued shares under (e) is not a reduction (s. 61(2)). VI. Address any connected notice under s. 64. VII. Conclude.
questionsAndAnswers.explanation: IRAC-style analysis aligned to the statutory text.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions on a Section 61 alteration contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Articles authorising the power; the general-meeting resolution; the precise clause of s. 61(1) invoked; voting-percentage analysis if consolidation/division; confirmation of paid/unpaid proportion if sub-division; statement that cancel of unissued is not a reduction; any Tribunal order or application; relief sought and connected filings under s. 64.

examTips: List the five types of alteration in s. 61(1)(a)–(e).
Tribunal only if consolidation/division changes voting percentage.
Sub-division must preserve the paid/unpaid proportion.
Cancel of unissued under (e) is not a reduction (s. 61(2)).
